get_battery_info.description: Read Key Light Mini battery state; a 404 means this capability is absent.

get_lights.description: Read power, brightness and the device's current CCT, HSV or scene state.

identify.description: Blink the selected light so the user can confirm which unit is being controlled.

set_brightness.description: Set brightness percent, preserving power and colour. Zero is legal but leaves on=1 with no visible output, so the control starts at 3.

brightness.description: Brightness percent; clamp client-side because firmware range behaviour differs.

set_color_temperature.description: Set CCT white point in mireds. Do not combine temperature with hue or saturation.

mireds.description: White point in mireds: 143 is about 7000 K and 344 about 2900 K. Keep native mireds rather than converting through an assumed linear Kelvin curve.

set_hsv.description: Set direct HSV colour on a Light Strip, ending any running scene. Deliberately not bound to the RGB-oriented generic colour role.

hue.description: Hue in whole degrees. The device stores 360 rather than folding it to 0.

saturation.description: Saturation in whole percent; fractional values are truncated by current firmware.

turn_off.description: Turn the light off. On a scene-running strip this also discards the scene, so Scene is read-only here.

turn_on.description: Turn the light on without changing its stored brightness or colour.

txt_match.description: The manufacturer value shared by this family.
Exclude the mutual-TLS Air MK.2 from this plain-HTTP specification.

methods.notes: Display name can be empty; fall back to the mDNS instance name in that case. TXT `id` is only a pre-HTTP dedupe hint, not a stable key.

mdns_txt_match.description: Manufacturer TXT value published by the classic lights and the Air MK.2; required first so another _elg._tcp product is not claimed.
Classic firmware publishes no tls TXT key. Air MK.2 publishes tls=CERT_1_VER_EN and speaks mutual-TLS WebSocket rather than HTTP.

identification.notes: TXT `dt` is a model hint, not a sufficient capability check: select CCT, HSV, scene and battery support from the response shapes declared in `variants`. TXT `id` is not reliably the MAC address. Use accessory-info.serialNumber as the durable identity.

device.name: Elgato Key Light classic HTTP family
device.notes:
Local control for classic Elgato lights over unauthenticated HTTP/JSON on TCP 9123. Covered are the Key Light, Key Light Air, Key Light MK.2, Key Light Neo, Key Light Mini, Ring Light, Light Strip and Light Strip Pro when they publish the classic HTTP surface. The Key Light Air MK.2 (board 214) is deliberately excluded: it uses mutual-TLS WebSocket JSON-RPC on the same port, not this API. A client distinguishes them by the absence of the mDNS `tls` TXT key here, never by guessing from the product name.
No cloud or pairing is needed for control. The HTTP surface is unauthenticated and effectively single-threaded: use one keep-alive connection per light and do not issue parallel requests. The same surface also exposes destructive operations, so only the declared commands should be sent. Range handling varies by model and neither rejects nor clamps consistently; clamp client-side to the declared ranges.

openness.notes: Only derived protocol facts are recorded here. Vendor application internals, proprietary firmware and signing material are not part of this specification. The live community results and the independent client implementations agree on the control surface below.

factory_reset.effect: Clears the Wi-Fi configuration so the light can be onboarded again. The two procedures below are vendor-documented for the named models; do not generalise their button location or timing to the whole family.

procedures.basis: Elgato's Key Light Mini — Reset Wi-Fi Configurations support article; not replayed by this project.
procedures.name: Key Light Mini Wi-Fi reset

steps.action: Power on the Key Light Mini.
Hold the recessed Reset button with a small tool for 10 seconds.
Release Reset and wait for the light to restart.
steps.expect: The light is ready to be onboarded again.

procedures.basis: Elgato's Key Light Neo — Reset Wi-Fi Configuration support article; not replayed by this project.
procedures.indicator: The light flashes three times, then restarts.
procedures.name: Key Light Neo Wi-Fi reset

steps.action: Power on the Key Light Neo.
Hold the recessed Reset button with a small tool for at least 10 seconds.
Release Reset and wait for the automatic restart.
steps.expect: The light is ready to be onboarded again.

methods.description: Join the light with the vendor Control Center application, then use local HTTP directly.
methods.name: Control Center onboarding

steps.action: Power the light and wait for its setup network or onboarding offer.
steps.expect: The light is ready to be adopted by Control Center.

steps.action: Follow the Control Center onboarding flow and choose the home Wi-Fi network.
Wait for the light to join the LAN.
steps.expect: An _elg._tcp.local. advertisement appears on TCP 9123 without a tls TXT key.

setup.notes: Initial onboarding uses the light's own setup network and the vendor Control Center flow. The classic wifi-info payload is obfuscated rather than securely encrypted; this spec does not claim an independent provisioning implementation. Once onboarded, control needs no account.

rejoin.notes: The documented Mini and Neo route to a new network is the Wi-Fi reset above. Reset procedures for the other models remain unverified here.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The cited community protocol characterisation exercised a Key Light Air, Key Light Mini and Light Strip live; the remaining model coverage is reported, not confirmed.

variants.notes: Key Light family and Ring Light: `on`, `brightness` and white-point `temperature` in mireds.
Light Strip in direct-colour mode: `on`, `brightness`, `hue` and `saturation`. Never add `temperature` to an HSV write.
A Light Strip running a scene. A bare power, brightness or colour write discards the running scene, so this entity is intentionally read-only.
Key Light Mini battery surface. Probe once: 200 means present, 404 means absent; the accessory-info features list does not report it.

entities.name: Key Light
entities.notes: Brightness is 3-100 in the control to avoid on=1 at zero output. White point stays in native mireds (143-344), not a mislabeled Kelvin slider.

entities.name: Light Strip
entities.notes: `set_hsv` declares the wire write but is not bound: the generic set_color role expects red/green/blue channels, not hue/saturation. A client with an HSV picker can bind it directly.

entities.name: Light Strip Scene
entities.notes: Read-only deliberately. A bare on/off, brightness or HSV write discards the running scene and there is no scene-list endpoint. Cache the full scene object before considering a restore command.

entities.name: Battery
entities.notes: Fractional percent; expect small fluctuations while charging. Probe the endpoint once and treat 404 as a final no-battery answer.

evidence.documentation_review: Reviewed 2026-10-31: the public matterbridge-elgato protocol characterisation (live Key Light Air, Key Light Mini and Light Strip), python-elgato, the Key Light Mini firmware reverse-engineering write-up, and the project's clean-room Elgato research notes. The mDNS, JSON field shapes, partial-write behaviour and range quirks agree. No vendor source symbols, proprietary images, real device identifiers or credentials are reproduced. All ordinary control commands are confirmed by the cited live community work; broader model coverage and firmware upload remain reported.
evidence.open_questions: The remaining work is scoped in remaining_unknowns: per-model reset procedures, independent provisioning, scene-preserving writes, battery enum coverage, firmware recovery and the separate Air MK.2 transport.

dfu_mode.notes: The light stays on its ordinary LAN address while chunks upload. No separate update-mode SSID or advertisement is documented.

enter.notes: The running application receives and validates the image through the prepare/data/execute endpoints; no separate bootloader mode is entered before upload.

image.format: Complete vendor image including its 128-byte little-endian header: board type, four u16 version components, payload size/offset, signature slot and a 64-byte signature. Signature input is SHA-512(header[0:64] || payload), signed with Ed25519.
image.notes: Only the vendor image for the exact board id is appropriate. No image or signing material is distributed with this spec.

recovery.notes: Community firmware analysis describes an inactive-slot update: the previous slot remains bootable until execute selects the new image after validation. Behaviour at every possible power-loss point has not been tested by this project.

http_endpoints.description: Product name, board id, serial number, display name, firmware and Wi-Fi metadata. Use serialNumber as identity, not mDNS TXT id.
http_endpoints.name: Accessory Information

http_endpoints.description: Returns {numberOfLights, lights:[...]}. Read lights[0]. CCT replies carry on/brightness/temperature; direct-colour replies carry on/brightness/hue/saturation; scene replies replace those colour fields with id/name/scene/numberOfSceneElements.
http_endpoints.name: Light State

fields.description: Power state, integer 0 or 1 (never a JSON boolean).
fields.name: on

fields.description: Brightness percent. Integer in ordinary modes; may be fractional in a scene.
fields.name: brightness

fields.description: CCT white point in mireds, useful range 143-344.
fields.name: temperature

http_endpoints.description: Accepts a partial lights array and preserves unnamed fields. Returns the complete new state, so a client can consume the PUT response instead of immediately issuing another GET.
http_endpoints.name: Set Light State

http_endpoints.description: Key Light Mini only: level (fractional percent), status (0 not charging, 1 pre-charge, 2 fast charge, 3 complete), powerSource (0 unknown, 1 USB, 2 battery), currentBatteryVoltage and inputChargeVoltage (mV), and inputChargeCurrent (mA). A 404 means no battery surface.
http_endpoints.name: Battery Information

http_endpoints.description: Blink the selected light. Empty request body.
http_endpoints.name: Identify

http_endpoints.advanced_reason: Erases the inactive firmware slot in preparation for replacement. Only a vendor image for the exact board should be supplied.
http_endpoints.description: Body {"size":N} with the complete image length including the 128-byte header. Allow at least 60 seconds.
http_endpoints.name: Firmware Update Prepare

http_endpoints.advanced_reason: Writes one 4096-byte firmware chunk. An incorrect or interrupted image can leave the light unavailable until recovery.
http_endpoints.description: Raw chunk at the byte offset in the query string. Chunks are sent in order with Connection: close; an accepted intermediate chunk answers 202. The last chunk answers 200 only after signature and checksum validation. A 400 or 408 means retry that chunk.
http_endpoints.name: Firmware Update Data

http_endpoints.advanced_reason: Selects the newly written firmware slot and restarts the light. Do not send until every chunk has been acknowledged.
http_endpoints.description: Empty body; validates and activates the staged image, then restarts.
http_endpoints.name: Firmware Update Execute

remaining_unknowns: Wi-Fi reset procedures for original Key Light, Key Light Air, Key Light MK.2, Ring Light, Light Strip and Light Strip Pro need vendor citations or hardware confirmation.
An independent provisioning client still needs the classic wifi-info key schedule reviewed for clean-room redistribution; steady-state control does not depend on it.
The full scene catalogue is not enumerable from the device. A safe scene-preserving write path should cache complete observed scenes first.
Battery charge-status values 0, 1 and 3, and powerSource 0 and 2, are from public prior art rather than the live Mini sample.
Firmware-update recovery at every power-loss point, and whether every classic model uses the same inactive-slot behaviour, remain untested by this project.
Air MK.2 mutual-TLS WebSocket control and BLE onboarding are outside this spec; its client-certificate issuance path is unresolved.
